story: Vishwamitra was a powerful king who tried to take the sage Vashishtha's wish-granting cow and lost. Humbled, he gave up his kingdom to become an even greater sage than Vashishtha, through thousands of years of penance. He later trained Rama and Lakshmana.
belief: He is the seer to whom the Gayatri Mantra, the most sacred mantra of Hinduism, was revealed. He shows that a person can rise beyond their birth through effort.
turns: His penance was broken again and again by his temper and desire, including by the apsara Menaka, with whom he had a daughter, Shakuntala. In some versions his rivalry led to the deaths of Vashishtha's hundred sons.
facts: He created a second heaven for King Trishanku when the gods refused to let him in.
Shakuntala's son Bharata is the king after whom India is named Bharat.
He finally became a brahmarishi, the highest rank of sage.
lessons: The hardest kingdom to conquer is your own ego.
You can rise beyond the circumstances of your birth.
Setbacks are part of the path.
more: He took the young Rama and Lakshmana to the forest to defeat the demoness Tataka.
He led Rama to the svayamvara where Rama broke Shiva's bow and won Sita.
